summary: The video side is a scan-time pipeline driven by H/V raster counters. Sprites go through a bus-request DMA, a per-line object search into a double line buffer, and a per-pixel draw. Tiles are fetched on HS[2:0] phases and the mixer is a PROM-style selector. None of it follows MAME's tilemap/draw_sprites/screen_update split. The main CPU, MCU and ADPCM CPU are modelled at pin and strobe level (BUSRQ/BUSAK, OKOUT, P3 pins, /MREQ wait states). The only things shared with MAME are bit layouts and the priority pen ranges, which any correct core has to match.

findings.note: H counts 0x80-0x1FF and V reloads at a start value, the way a 74161 counter chain does. Blanking, the object timing signals LHBL_obj/LVBL_obj (two lines ahead) and sync all come from compares on these counters. MAME only uses a scanline-number callback.

The OKOUT write strobe drives bus_req into the real Z80 busrq_n. busak_n enables a line counter (blen) that walks the CPU RAM address bus (RAM_addr mux on blcnten). MAME instead calls buffered_spriteram copy() and runs a timer.

findings.signal: per-line object search + double line buffer
findings.note: Each line, a SEARCH/TRANSFER machine compares Y with the line (Vsum = Y + ~VF) and copies up to OBJMAX_LINE objects into a ping-pong line RAM, which is cleared on readout. MAME's version is a per-frame loop over the whole of spriteram in reverse.

findings.signal: pixel-clocked object draw with adder-style Y compare
findings.note: pxlcnt phases latch ID, attributes, Y and X in turn. Y is matched with a two's-complement adder (~VF + flip + Y). ROM planes are shifted out one pixel per cen into posx-addressed line-buffer writes, not blitted per sprite.
The ID bits {7,5,6}, color bits 3:1, Trojan hflip=bit4/vflip=1 and Avengers vflip=~bit4 are the same as MAME's bitswap<3>(7,5,6) and orientation split. A correct core has to share this data layout.

findings.signal: tile fetch phased on HS bits
findings.note: Scroll sums are built from H/V and gate-level terms such as H7 = (~Hfix[8] & (~flip ^ HF[6])) ^ HF[7]. The ROM address is latched when HS[2:0]==1 and pixels are shifted out of 4 plane registers. MAME uses tile_info callbacks feeding its tilemap engine.

findings.signal: BG2 map read from ROM during scan
findings.note: The map ROM address is computed on the pixel clock from {row,col} plus hpos[15:8]<<4 (the image register). It ends up at the same address as MAME's row*0x800|col*2 + image*0x20, but is built as a scan-time address generator, not a tilemap mapper with mark_all_dirty.

Each pixel's char-opaque, obj-opaque, BG1 group bit, BG1 color and BG1-blank bits are packed into an 8-bit seladdr, which a combinational function decodes into a 2-bit layer select, much like a priority PROM. MAME draws the layers in sequence (bg2, bg1 layer1, sprites, bg1 layer0, fg).

BG1 pens 7-11 with group bit set beat sprites, and BG1 pen 0 falls through to BG2. These are exactly MAME's transmask ranges, written as fixed equations instead of a loaded PROM. A PROM would give the same result, so this signal is weak.

findings.signal: Z80 wait-state and interrupt vector at bus level
findings.note: Avengers inserts one wait state on each /MREQ falling edge outside refresh, which MAME does not model. The IRQ vector is placed on the data bus (0xD7) during IORQ&M1, and the interrupt is a latch set on the LVBL edge and cleared by acknowledge. The interrupt scheme also departs from MAME's V128 IRQ / line-248 NMI callbacks.

The 8751's P3 inputs are wired to ~mrd, LVBL and an INT0 latch set by the main-CPU write and cleared on a P3.7 toggle. P1 is wired to the V counter, and a P3.6 rising edge strobes the p0/p2 output latches. The semantics match MAME's handlers, but the code is organised as pins and latches.
The casez address decode and the F80E bit assignments (flip, bank, NMI mask, sound reset) agree with MAME's address map. Any correct core has to share them.
